rationale: This is a sign-flipped cosmetic variant of the archived "Stop-Go R&D Financing Volatility" (same two volatility legs), and the archive already showed that high R&D-vol × high liability-vol earned *positive* alpha, so simply negating the liability-vol leg contradicts the existing evidence rather than diagnosing it.

Stripped of the goodwill tweak this is plain book leverage — a long-published, heavily-studied characteristic — and since goodwill is a small share of assets for most firms the adjustment leaves the signal nearly rank-identical to lt/at, making it both a rediscovery and a non-cross-theme single ratio.

The time-series high-watermark conditioning (TS_RANK of own goodwill history) is a genuinely different conditioner from the cross-sectional IND_RANK/ACCEL versions already tested, and the dlc-vs-dltt growth spread is a cleaner maturity-deterioration measure, though it remains an incremental third pass at a rollover-goodwill family that has so far produced negligible FF5 alpha.

This is essentially the archived "Long-Maturity Organic Runway" with the deflator changed from at to lt, xrd/sale to xrd/at, and the goodwill leg dropped — a scaling/simplification variant of a construct that already returned ls_talpha 0.74 and a wrong-signed FMB slope, with no new economic content.

Nearly identical to the archived "Liability Growth R&D Retrenchment" apart from a one-period lag and an at-vs-sale deflator, and that prior version produced a *significantly positive* FMB slope (t=2.55) against a negative expected sign, so re-proposing it with the same negative prior ignores rather than diagnoses the contradicting evidence.

The pairing of liability-growth with advertising-intensity volatility is a combination not yet tested (prior versions used an ad-minus-R&D mix or a debt-maturity volatility spread), but both legs are individually recycled and the archive's volatility-leg signals have tended to load positively, so the negative expected sign is at real risk of reversing.
